## Design

### 2026-09-30 — I started with a simple idea: an Arduino that sounds a buzzer when water leaks from a pipe. I asked for a parts list, then checked which programming language and editor I'd use, and found out it's C++

**2h**

I started with a simple idea: an Arduino that sounds a buzzer when water leaks from a pipe. I asked for a parts list, then checked which programming language and editor I'd use, and found out it's C++ and that either the Arduino IDE or VS Code with PlatformIO would work. After that,

![image_2026-09-30_202224210](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ZB18468vV6xymMeGfUgN9PiGVu6vR4in/b3930d37fe97e7ed6947ad92ca7f5053f63abac3c5a64dcbca102b65c6801ace.png)

 I went through the actual listings one at a time and checked each against the project. The water leak sensor with the 3.5mm plug turned out to be two bare probes on a cable, which suits the job because I can put them under a pipe while the board stays dry. Since the Uno has no 3.5mm socket, I learned I needed a breakout board and compared a screw-terminal one with the CJMCU TRRS one. I confirmed the ATmega328P Uno R3 clone runs the same code as the official board, and that the 400-point breadboard has plenty of room for the buzzer and wiring. The only thing still on my list is a pack of male-to-male jumper wires, which none of those listings clearly include.
